prompt:
Model a two-leaf hinge, lying open and flat, as the two parts `leaf_a` and `leaf_b`.

The hinge line is the X axis at z = 7 mm. Every interface number is already in the project's `globals.py` - read them through `hc` instead of repeating them. Each leaf is a flat plate 20 mm wide (X), 30 mm deep (Y) and 4 mm thick, lying on the XY plane with its underside at z = 0, plus a single knuckle: a 10 mm diameter barrel, 20 mm long, centred on the hinge axis and spanning the same 20 mm of X as its own plate - the barrel rides above the plate (its underside 2 mm off the table) and the plate merges into the barrel's flank so the leaf is one solid. `leaf_a` sits on the -Y side of the axis with its plate and knuckle spanning x = -20 to x = 0; `leaf_b` mirrors it on the +Y side spanning x = 0 to x = 20, so the two knuckle end faces meet flush at x = 0. Bore a 6 mm diameter pin hole through each knuckle along the hinge axis. Each plate's inner edge stops 3.5 mm short of the axis - the plates keep a 7 mm swing gap across the joint.

Tag the mating interfaces on each leaf: the pin bore wall as `pin_bore`, the knuckle end face at x = 0 as `mate_face`, and the plate's inner edge face (the one facing the other leaf) as `swing_edge`. Assembly checking addresses the leaves through exactly those names.

The project also seeds an inspection gauge part (`pin_gauge`, a 5.9 mm go-pin on the hinge axis) that the acceptance fits through both bores - leave it exactly as it is.

Build both leaves and export each as STEP when the geometry is right.

entry.note: one pin must pass both knuckles: the bores share the hinge axis
the knuckle end faces meet flush at x = 0, facing each other
the plates stand off 3.5 mm each side of the axis so the hinge can fold
